verdicts.reason: Both use the same broken layout. One giant can stands in for the trio, the three flavour names sit in a stacked list cut off from their descriptors (which are mismatched and in a different order), the CTA is shrunk to an unreadable pill at the bottom, and two thumbnail cans float beside it. A wins only because its CTA reads 'Build Your Pack'; B's reads 'Build YourPack' and its CTA text is even tinier.

A moves the CTA up to a large, readable pill at top right. It is jammed against the logo and has a missing space ('YourPack'), but at least it is visible. B's CTA is a tiny, illegible pill at the bottom. Both share the same core failures: one oversized can, a flavour list split from its mismatched descriptors, and stray mini-cans at the bottom.

B keeps the original structure: logo, headline, three cans each with its own name and descriptor in the right order, then the tagline and CTA. Its flaws: the headline and descriptors are small for the canvas, the can labels are illegible, and there is a lot of dead space. A breaks the design with one giant can, a mismatched flavour/descriptor list, a tiny CTA ('YourPack') and orphaned mini-cans.

B faithfully adapts the three-can row and keeps a clear reading order. Its type is undersized and the can labels can't be read, but it is coherent. A puts a readable CTA at top right, crowded next to the logo, but still has the giant single can, flavour names split from their reordered descriptors, and two tiny stray cans at the bottom.
